meta.question: Does accumulating per-event deposited energy per sugar-phosphate site (then thresholding once) — the physically-faithful Nikjoo/Charlton model — raise direct SSB toward the P=1 limit and pull the ratio back into PARTRAC's band?
meta.method: Same fresh v0.7.0 GPU dump + rad_e as E31; direct scorer now SUMS each event's deposit into its nearest (bp,strand) site and thresholds once with the ramp. Node IRT + SSB, N=4096/10 keV.

finding: HYPOTHESIS REFUTED. Accumulation did NOT raise direct SSB (27 vs 30 per-event; within noise). Diagnosis: the 93 in-reach events map to ~90 DISTINCT sugars — near-backbone sugars are almost all hit by a SINGLE ionisation because the 0.29 nm reaction radius is too small for deposits to overlap. So per-event and accumulated are equivalent here. The gap to PARTRAC's 2-3 band is therefore NOT the per-event approximation — it is the ENERGY THRESHOLD itself: requiring >5-37.5 eV makes a single water ionisation break a sugar only ~1/3 of the time (mean deposit ~15 eV). The P=1 limit (2.32) is the outlier that happens to hit the band; both energy-threshold variants give ~6.5-7.1.
implication: To reconcile a first-principles energy-threshold direct model with PARTRAC, the lever is the threshold values and/or the effective sugar-phosphate reaction volume (0.29 nm radius may be too small to capture the relevant deposit), NOT the per-event-vs-accumulated aggregation. Both remain parameter-free; this is an honest-negative that localizes the discrepancy.
status: pass (implemented + validated); honest-negative — accumulation hypothesis refuted, gap localized to the threshold/volume
